summary: This script syncs blog posts to an AnythingLLM workspace by checking file hashes to detect new and modified posts, then uploading only those that have changed. It maintains a state file to remember which posts have been indexed and their locations in the workspace, so subsequent runs skip unchanged files. The script also handles removing old versions of modified posts before uploading the new ones, and embeds publication dates and URLs into the document metadata.

explanations.10: These three lines make the script fail immediately if any command returns an error, if any variable is undefined, or if a pipe fails anywhere in a chain—this prevents silent failures.
explanations.14: This uses the bash syntax '${VAR:-default}' which means: use the ANYTHINGLLM_WORKSPACE environment variable if it exists, otherwise use the string 'blog' as a fallback.
explanations.22: This checks if the API key wasn't provided as an environment variable AND a .env file exists, then it tries to extract the API key from that file.
explanations.23: This finds the line starting with 'ANYTHINGLLM_API_KEY=', takes the first match, splits on the equals sign and keeps everything after it, then removes any quote characters.
explanations.25: This is a special bash idiom: if the API key is empty or unset, the script stops and prints the error message as a reminder of where to get the key.
explanations.30: The script tries two possible URLs to find AnythingLLM—one works when running on the Docker host, the other works when running from inside another container.
explanations.39: This defines a helper function that wraps curl and automatically adds the API authorization header to every request.
explanations.48: This awk script starts looking for YAML frontmatter (the dashed lines at the top of Markdown) and extracts a specific key's value when found.
explanations.68: The script reads the previous state file into an associative array (like a dictionary/map) where the key is the file path and the value contains the file's hash and its location in AnythingLLM.
explanations.71: This reads the state file line-by-line, splitting each line on a tab character into hash, path, and location.
explanations.82: The '-d \0' makes read use null bytes as delimiters instead of newlines, so it can handle filenames with spaces or special characters correctly.
explanations.83: This computes a SHA256 checksum of the file, then extracts just the hash part (before the space).
explanations.85: This extracts the known hash from the previous state by taking everything before the first tab character.
explanations.99: The script pulls the slug (URL-friendly name) from the post's frontmatter metadata at the top of the Markdown file.
explanations.100: If no slug was defined in the metadata, use the folder name as a fallback, since each post is stored in its own directory.
explanations.110: The script pulls the publication date from the Markdown frontmatter and appends it to the title, since AnythingLLM records upload date instead of written date.
explanations.115: If this post was previously indexed, extract its old location so we can delete the stale version before uploading the new one.
explanations.116: This extracts the document location from the previous state by taking everything after the first tab character.
explanations.125: This makes an HTTP POST request to upload the Markdown file to AnythingLLM's document upload endpoint with metadata attached.
explanations.126: The file is sent as form data with a custom filename (the slug) and marked as Markdown type so AnythingLLM processes it correctly.
explanations.128: The metadata is sent as JSON containing the title, source file path, and a special 'chunkSource' link that tells AnythingLLM what URL to cite.
explanations.134: This extracts the location field from AnythingLLM's response JSON, which identifies where the document was stored in the workspace.
explanations.149: This finds all index.md and index.mdx files recursively, uses '-print0' to handle special characters safely, and pipes them sorted to the while loop.
explanations.152: After processing all files, this rewrites the state file from scratch with only the posts that were successfully processed, so deleted posts disappear from tracking.
explanations.155: The state file is rewritten sorted by file path so it's consistent and readable for debugging.
